sources.brief_claim_check: differs: the number resolves to a genuine Commission Implementing Regulation, but its legal basis is Article 13(5) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR) and its subject is the DPP registry; it is NOT the implementing act required by Article 77(9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542.
uncertainties: Text was read through a summarising fetch tool at the Publications Office Cellar because every EUR-Lex URL returned empty content; wording here is paraphrase and was not character-verified.

The act contains a heading 'Article 6a' (Transfer of registered digital product passports) between Articles 6 and 7 although it is a newly adopted act; confirmed in two separate reads but unusual, so article numbering should be re-checked against the OJ PDF.
No separate date of application was found: Art. 24 is headed 'Entry into force' only. Articles 1-5 were read in the first 100000 characters and Articles 5-24 in the remainder; no annexes were seen.
Commission web pages state the registry became operational on 20 July 2026, which is before this act's entry into force on 6 August 2026; the relationship between those two dates was not resolved.

Art. 8(7)(a) and (c) were reported as referring to 'applicable delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 77 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542' or other Union law; this phrasing should be re-read in the OJ PDF before being encoded as a rule.
Cellar metadata lists an end-of-validity date of 9999-12-31 (open-ended).

provisions.summary: Every LMT battery, industrial battery above 2 kWh capacity and electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service must have an electronic record called a battery passport.
provisions.applies_to: LMT batteries; industrial batteries with capacity greater than 2 kWh; electric vehicle batteries
provisions.conditions: Threshold of more than 2 kWh applies to industrial batteries only

provisions.summary: The passport holds battery-model information and information specific to the individual battery, including use data, as listed in Annex XIII, in three access tiers: public (Annex XIII point 1); notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission (points 2 and 3); persons with a legitimate interest (points 2 and 4). The Commission may amend Annex XIII by delegated act under Art. 89.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport data set and its access tiers
provisions.conditions: Access for persons with a legitimate interest depends on the implementing acts under Art. 77(9)

provisions.summary: The passport is reached through the QR code of Art. 13(6), which links to a unique identifier attributed by the economic operator placing the battery on the market; the QR code and identifier must comply with ISO/IEC 15459 parts 1 to 6 or their equivalent, a list the Commission may update by delegated act.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the battery on the market; data carrier and unique identifier
provisions.conditions: Equivalent standards allowed; empowerment to amend the list of standards

provisions.summary: The economic operator placing the battery on the market must keep passport information accurate, complete and up to date, and may give another operator written authorisation to act on its behalf.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the battery on the market
provisions.conditions: Written authorisation required for delegation

provisions.summary: Passport information must be based on open standards, in an interoperable format, transferable, machine-readable, structured and searchable in line with the essential requirements of Art. 78; access is regulated in line with Art. 78.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport data format and access
provisions.conditions: Refers to Art. 78

provisions.summary: After preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing, responsibility for the passport passes to the operator that places the resulting battery on the market or puts it into service, and that battery gets a new passport linked to the original one or ones. When a battery becomes waste, responsibility passes to the producer, the producer responsibility organisation or the waste management operator.
provisions.applies_to: Operators of re-used, repurposed and remanufactured batteries; producers, PROs, waste management operators
provisions.conditions: Change of status of the battery

provisions.summary: The battery passport ceases to exist once the battery has been recycled.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport lifecycle
provisions.conditions: Recycling of the battery

provisions.version_examined: Consolidated version 02023R1542-20260813 (paragraph carries no amendment marker)
provisions.summary: The Commission must adopt implementing acts specifying who counts as a person with a legitimate interest for Art. 77(2)(c), which information they may access, and how far they may download, share, publish and re-use it. Criteria: the information is needed to assess the status and residual value of the battery, or for preparation for re-use, repurposing, remanufacturing or recycling choices, and access to commercially sensitive information is kept to the minimum necessary. Examination procedure of Art. 90(3).
provisions.applies_to: European Commission; persons with a legitimate interest; Annex XIII points 2 and 4
provisions.conditions: Examination procedure under Art. 90(3), which points to Art. 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. As of 2026-10-13 no adopted act was located.

provisions.version_examined: Consolidated version 02023R1542-20260813 (inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, as corrected by C2)
provisions.summary: The responsible economic operator must upload the battery's unique identifier to the registry established under Art. 13(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the battery on the market
provisions.applicable_from: Not stated in the paragraph as read; tied to the battery passport obligation (2027-02-18) and to the registry rules of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778
provisions.conditions: Depends on the ESPR registry

provisions.summary: Essential requirements for the technical design and operation of the passport: full interoperability with other digital product passports under Union ecodesign law; free-of-charge access according to the access rights in Annex XIII and the Art. 77(9) act; data stored by the responsible operator or operators authorised to act for it; authorised operators may not sell, re-use or process the data beyond the service; passport stays available after the responsible operator ceases to exist or to operate in the Union; rights to access, introduce, modify or update information restricted per Annex XIII and the Art. 77(9) act; data authentication, reliability and integrity ensured; high level of security and privacy and fraud avoided.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport systems and the operators running them
provisions.conditions: Points (b) and (f) depend on the Art. 77(9) implementing act, not located as adopted

provisions.version_examined: Consolidated version 02023R1542-20260813 (point 1(q) carries corrigendum marker C4)
provisions.summary: Point 1 lists publicly accessible battery-model information in items (a) to (s), including Annex VI Part A information, material composition, carbon footprint, responsible sourcing, recycled content, renewable content share, rated capacity, voltage, power capability, expected lifetime, temperature range, warranty period, round-trip efficiency, internal resistance, C-rate, marking requirements, EU declaration of conformity and waste prevention and management information. Point 2 lists model information for persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission in items (a) to (d): detailed composition, part numbers and spare-part sources, dismantling information, safety measures. Point 3 is the results of test reports proving compliance, for notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission. Point 4 lists individual-battery information for persons with a legitimate interest in items (a) to (d): performance and durability parameter values, state of health, battery status, and use data.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport data set by access tier
provisions.applicable_from: 2027-02-18 (with Art. 77(1)); individual items follow the application dates of the provisions they reference
provisions.conditions: Item (k) of point 1 concerns electric vehicle batteries only

provisions.summary: Entry into force on the twentieth day after publication; general application from 18 February 2024, with Art. 11 from 18 February 2027, Art. 17 and Chapter VI from 18 August 2024 (Art. 17(2) later), and Chapter VIII from 18 August 2025.
provisions.applies_to: Whole Regulation
provisions.conditions: Staggered dates as listed; many articles carry their own internal dates

provisions.summary: Adopted under Art. 13(5), second subparagraph, read with the third subparagraph, of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781.
provisions.applies_to: The act as a whole

provisions.summary: Sets the implementation arrangements for the ESPR Art. 13 registry for economic operators placing on the market or putting into service products that need a digital product passport and a registry entry: products under ESPR delegated acts, batteries (Art. 77 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542), construction products (Regulation (EU) 2024/3110), toys (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509), detergents and surfactants (Regulation (EU) 2026/405) and any other product so required by Union law. Also covers registry use by value chain actors, national and customs authorities and the Commission.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operators, value chain actors, authorities, Commission; batteries expressly in scope under point (b)
provisions.conditions: Without prejudice to specific rules in other Union law (recital 2)

provisions.summary: For this act, 'digital product passport' includes the battery passport under Art. 77 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. Seventeen further terms are defined, including verified economic operator, semantic repository, semantic conformity, data model and hash of the passport version.
provisions.applies_to: Interpretation of the act

provisions.summary: Verified status lasts until the electronic identification means expire and at most three years from verification.
provisions.applies_to: Verified economic operators and value chain actors
provisions.conditions: Maximum three years

provisions.summary: Member States must appoint a designated national administrator at the latest by 18 February 2027.
provisions.applies_to: Member States

provisions.summary: A verified economic operator placing the product on the market or putting it into service registers the passport: for ESPR products at the model, batch or item level set by the delegated act; for batteries and the other non-ESPR product groups at the level set by the relevant Union law, with third-party registration allowed where that law permits and the third party is verified. Where several rules apply, the most granular level governs; item-level passports link to batch and model identifiers where they exist. Registration is made through the registry user interface or its API.
provisions.applies_to: Verified economic operators; batteries under Art. 1(1)(b)
provisions.conditions: Granularity for batteries follows Regulation (EU) 2023/1542

provisions.summary: On submission the registry automatically checks semantic conformity, consistency of mandatory registry data with the passport where relevant, the required granularity level, validity of the commodity code where relevant, and that the link to the service-provider back-up works where relevant. After a successful check it generates a unique persistent registration identifier, stores identifiers, commodity code, service-provider reference and registrant data with date and time, and returns the registration identifier to the registrant.
provisions.applies_to: Registry operation; registrants
provisions.conditions: Points (a) and (c) of paragraph 7 were reported as referring to delegated acts under ESPR, under Art. 77 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, or other Union law; wording to be re-read

provisions.summary: The registrant can generate a downloadable proof of registration showing the product identifier, commodity code where relevant, operator identity, registration date and time with a Commission time stamp and a hash of the passport version, secured by a qualified electronic seal; it stays available for 90 calendar days from generation.
provisions.applies_to: Registering economic operators and third parties acting for them
provisions.conditions: 90 calendar days availability (Art. 9(4))

provisions.summary: Registration data is deleted automatically ten years after registration unless Union law sets a different period.
provisions.applies_to: Registry data
provisions.conditions: Other Union law may set another period

provisions.summary: Passport data must follow the common, versioned data models held in the semantic repository, which derive from ESPR delegated acts or other applicable Union law. The Commission maintains the repository as an authoritative machine-readable source of attribute meanings, data models and formats, DCAT-AP metadata, role meanings and multilingual labels, with search and public APIs, free of charge.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operators' passport data; Commission

provisions.summary: The Commission evaluates the act by the end of 2032 and every six years thereafter. The act enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication and is binding and directly applicable.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; the act as a whole
provisions.conditions: No separate application date found

provisions.citation: Art. 1, Art. 2 and Annex; recitals 1, 2 and 6
provisions.summary: Publishes in the Official Journal the references of six harmonised standards for digital product passports drafted under standardisation request C(2024) 5423 as amended by C(2025) 8024: EN 18216:2026, EN 18219:2026, EN 18220:2026, EN 18221:2026, EN 18222:2026 and EN 18223:2026. Conformity with them gives a presumption of conformity with Arts 10 and 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (per its Art. 41(2)) from the date of publication. Enters into force on the day of publication.
provisions.applies_to: Digital product passports under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781
provisions.conditions: Presumption is under the ESPR, not under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542; no restrictions reported

provisions.summary: Publishes in the Official Journal the reference of one harmonised standard for batteries, EN 18060:2025, drafted in support of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. Recital 1 recalls that conformity with cited harmonised standards gives a presumption of conformity with Arts 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and 78 of that Regulation to the extent covered. Enters into force on the day of publication.
provisions.applies_to: Batteries under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542
provisions.conditions: Extent of coverage by the standard not examined; the decision does not mention the battery passport or Art. 77

anomalies: No page examined contained text addressed to an AI or automated agent.

All EUR-Lex URLs (ELI, TXT/HTML, ALL) returned empty content to the fetch tool; all legislative text was read at the Publications Office Cellar (publications.europa.eu), the official repository behind EUR-Lex.
All page content was read through a summarising fetch tool, so text in this file is paraphrase and titles may have small transcription differences.

One Cellar manifestation URL returned a ZIP archive that the harness saved automatically to its tool-results folder; it was not requested as a download, was not opened, and nothing in this file relies on it.
Cellar expression numbering is not stable across works: '.0006' was English for the 2026 acts but Greek for the consolidated Batteries Regulation, where English was '.0007'.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 contains an 'Article 6a' although it is an original act.
Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 entered into force on 6 August 2026, while Commission pages say the DPP registry became operational on 20 July 2026.
The brief treats 2026/1778 as a candidate for the Article 77(9) act; it is the ESPR registry act. Batteries are nevertheless in its scope (Art. 1(1)(b)).

The brief does not mention Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2048 (EN 18060:2025 under the Batteries Regulation) or Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 (amends the Batteries Regulation; consolidated version 2026-08-13), both found during this audit.
The Commission DPP timeline as returned lists a delegated act for DPP service providers twice (Q2 2027 and Q3 2027).
Non-official search summaries disagree on whether a draft access-rights act was circulated to the Commission expert group in April 2026.
The fetch summary of the DG Environment page associated notice C/2025/214 with two different subjects (derogation calls and removability guidelines).
open_questions: Has a draft of the Article 77(9) access-rights implementing act been published on 'Have your say' or in the comitology register since September 2026? Neither portal could be read with the available tools.
Which access rules should the engine apply to Annex XIII points 2 and 4 on 18 February 2027 if the Article 77(9) act is still not in force by then?
Has a Commission implementing decision citing EN 18239:2026 and EN 18246:2026 been adopted? The Commission timeline said September 2026; none located as of 2026-10-13.

Does Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 set any application date different from its entry into force, and how does that relate to the registry being operational from 20 July 2026? The OJ PDF should be read in full.
What exactly does Art. 8(7) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 require for batteries, given that it reportedly refers to delegated acts under Art. 77 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542?
Which provisions of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 were changed by Regulation (EU) 2026/1738 and by corrigenda C3 and C4, beyond Annex I and Annex XIII point 1(q)?

Commission FAQ answer 7.3 (due diligence report required from August 2027) versus Art. 96(2)(c) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 as read in the consolidated text (Chapter VIII applies from 18 August 2025): reconcile against M2 Regulation (EU) 2025/1561, which was not read in this audit. This affects Annex XIII point 1(d).
Is the Commission data-point guidance still at V2 (15 August 2026), and what do its own cover page and disclaimer say? The PDF was not opened.

Do the six cited DPP standards give any presumption of conformity for battery passports under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542? Decision 2026/1736 grants it only for Arts 10 and 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781; Decision 2026/2048 cites only EN 18060:2025 under the Batteries Regulation.
